speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, which specific antibiotic were you taking when these symptoms of fever, itchy rash, and joint pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced serum sickness-like reaction.

I have noted the patient is an 8-year-old girl with a 2-day history of fever, itchy rash, and joint pain starting one week after taking amoxicillin for acute sinusitis. The rash progression from antecubital and popliteal fossae to the trunk is highly characteristic; do you or your child have any history of similar reactions to penicillin or sulfonamides?
